legal.headline: Law firm name not family property: Calcutta HC bars Somabrata Mandal from claiming connection with Fox & Mandal
legal.hook: Law firm name not family property: Calcutta HC bars Somabrata Mandal from claiming connection with Fox & Mandal
legal.summary: The Calcutta High Court has barred Somabrata Mandal from claiming any connection with or using the name of the law firm Fox & Mandal. The court ruled that a law firm's name is not family property and cannot be treated as a heritable or transferable asset. Mandal apparently sought to assert some claim or right over the firm's name, possibly following a dispute with other partners or successors. The judgment clarifies that partnership firm names are distinct legal entities and intellectual property matters, not personal or family property subject to inheritance or personal rights. The court's decision prevents Mandal from leveraging the firm's established reputation or brand identity. The ruling establishes that departing or former partners cannot unilaterally claim continued association with a law firm or its goodwill after separation.
legal.contextNote: This judgment addresses the nature of partnership firm assets under Indian partnership law (Partnership Act, 1932) and intellectual property principles. Law firm names represent goodwill, brand equity, and client trust—treated as firm assets, not personal property divisible among partners or heirs. The ruling matters for partnership disputes, succession planning, and firm restructuring. For practitioners: when advising on law firm splits, M&A of legal practices, or partner exits, ensure partnership deeds clearly define ownership of firm names, marks, and client lists. This precedent protects firms from former partners misappropriating brand identity post-separation. Lawyers should audit partnership agreements to prevent similar disputes and understand that courts will not treat law firm names as heritable family assets—critical for succession and dispute resolution planning.
